detailed_description: The Calendar Heatmap Generator is a specialized data visualization tool that transforms time-series datasets into color-coded calendar grids using HTML5 Canvas and SVG rendering. By mapping numerical values to chromatic gradients via D3.js scale interpolators, it enables granular analysis of daily patterns across months or years. Developers and analysts can input structured data in CSV/JSON formats containing ISO 8601 date stamps and corresponding metric values, which the tool processes through a date-fns.js parser to construct two-dimensional temporal matrices. Each calendar cell's fill color intensity is calculated using either linear or logarithmic color scales, with optional custom domain ranges for precise data normalization. The resulting visualizations support responsive SVG output with embedded metadata tooltips and raster PNG exports at 4K resolution. This tool addresses specific needs for tracking metrics like API usage trends, health tracking adherence, or financial transaction frequencies, offering precise control over date range filtering, color palette inversion, and weekday/weekend contrast adjustments.
usage_steps: Upload structured data via the file input field, ensuring columns contain 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD) and 'value' (numerical) fields
Select date range using the dual-month picker to define visualization boundaries
Configure color scale using the gradient builder with options for sequential, diverging, or custom hex color arrays
Adjust intensity normalization with the domain range slider to compress or expand color value mappings
Toggle weekday/weekend cell borders using the accessibility checkbox for temporal pattern emphasis
Export rendered visualization using the resolution selector (SVG or PNG with DPI control)
usage_examples: Analyzing daily GitHub commit frequency over six months to identify coding productivity patterns
Visualizing website traffic metrics from Google Analytics exports to detect seasonal user engagement trends
Tracking fitness app workout completion rates with color gradients showing exercise consistency
Mapping retail sales transactions to calendar days for identifying peak purchasing periods by week and month
